2027-02-10.title: Wednesday of the first week of the Great Fast · Anniversary of the Syro-Malankara Major Archiepiscopal Church
readings: A flaming torch passes between the pieces
I press on toward the goal
But who do you say that I am?
2027-02-10.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), first week. Anniversary of the raising of the Syro-Malankara Catholic Church to a Major Archiepiscopal Church (10 February 2005).
2027-02-10.verse: He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?” Peter answered, “The Messiah of God.”
theo: The covenant with Abram is sealed in the dark: “When the sun had gone down and it was dark, a smoking fire pot and a flaming torch passed between these pieces. On that day the Lord made a covenant with Abram.” Only God passes between the halves of the sacrifice; Abram does nothing but watch. In the ancient custom, those who passed between the pieces bound themselves to keep the covenant. Here God binds himself alone. The promise rests on his faithfulness, not ours. Paul, who knew that faithfulness, still says: “Not that I have already obtained this or have already reached the goal; but I press on to make it my own, because Christ Jesus has made me his own… forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead, I press on toward the goal for the prize of the heavenly call of God in Christ Jesus.” The Fast is that pressing on.

In the Gospel Jesus is praying alone and asks his disciples: “Who do the crowds say that I am?” Then the question that matters: “But who do you say that I am?” Peter answers: “The Messiah of God.” Today our Church gives thanks for its own place in that confession. On 10 February 2005 Pope John Paul II raised the Syro-Malankara Catholic Church to the rank of a Major Archiepiscopal Church, with Moran Mor Cyril Baselios as its first Major Archbishop; it is now led by Moran Mor Baselios Cardinal Cleemis, Major Archbishop-Catholicos. A Church that came home to communion with the See of Peter in 1930 was recognised as a Church with its own head and synod within that communion. The torch of God's faithfulness has passed through our history; we press on, confessing with Peter that Jesus is the Messiah of God.

2027-02-10.prayer: Lord God, faithful to your covenant, you passed through the darkness to bind yourself to Abram and his children. We thank you for our Syro-Malankara Catholic Church and for the gift of its Major Archiepiscopal dignity in communion with the Successor of Peter. Bless our Major Archbishop-Catholicos and our Holy Synod. Help us to press on toward the goal, confessing that Jesus is the Messiah of God. Amen.
altar: In every Holy Qurbono we pray for the Pope of Rome and for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos: one confession of faith, one Body of Christ.

quick: God alone passed between the pieces: his covenant rests on his faithfulness.

2027-02-10.question: Who do I say that Jesus is, not in words but in my choices?

family.explain: Jesus asked his friends: who do you say I am? Peter said: you are the Messiah, the Christ of God. Our Church today thanks God that it is one family with Peter's successor, the Pope.
family.intention: We pray for the Pope, for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos and for all our bishops.
family.ask: Ask: “If Jesus asked me, ‘Who am I for you?’, what would I say?”

illus: An old catechism teacher in Thiruvananthapuram kept two photographs above her desk: one of Mar Ivanios, who led the reunion of 1930, and one of the crowd at Pattom on the day the Major Archiepiscopal Church was celebrated in 2005. She told her students: the first man walked a hard road so that we could stand in that crowd. Your road will also be hard. Keep walking.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the Messiah of God. Make us confess you with our lips and our lives. Amen.
share: A flaming torch passed between these pieces (Genesis 15:17). Where have I seen God's faithfulness in my life?
Forgetting what lies behind (Philippians 3:13). What past do I need to let go?
But who do you say that I am? (Luke 9:20). What is my answer today?
pm.resp: Lord, keep us faithful to you.
interc: For Pope Leo and for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos.
For the Holy Synod and all the eparchies of our Church in India and abroad.
For the unity of all the Churches of the Malankara tradition.
For our priests and religious, that they may press on toward the goal.
For our parish as we keep the first week of the Great Fast.
pm.close: Father, you have been faithful to our Church through all its history. Keep us one in the faith of Peter, pressing on toward the heavenly call in Christ Jesus. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, the covenant with Abram was sealed at night: a smoking fire pot and a flaming torch passed between the pieces (Genesis 15:17). God alone passed through. His promise rests on his faithfulness, not ours.
Paul says: not that I have already reached the goal; but forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead, I press on (Philippians 3:12–14). The Fast is our pressing on.
Jesus asks his disciples: but who do you say that I am? Peter answers: the Messiah of God (Luke 9:20). Every Christian must give that answer personally.

Today our Church thanks God for 10 February 2005, when it was raised to a Major Archiepiscopal Church in communion with the See of Peter. Let us pray for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos and Synod, and press on together, confessing Christ. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus asked: who do you say I am? Peter said: you are the Christ! Today our Church says thank you to God for making us a big family together with the Pope. Can you say to Jesus today: you are my Lord?
